title: حِكَايَةُ السِّمْسَارِ النَّصْرَانِيِّ
titleEn: The Christian Broker's Tale, continued: the Young Man with the Severed Hand and the Woman of Cairo
part: Night 26 · The Christian Broker's Tale, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 211–217 (Night 26, continuing directly from nights-25), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 26 carries on the Christian broker's tale to the King. The young merchant tells how the woman of Cairo received him, how he spent his money on her night after night until he had nothing, and how, in despair, he tried to pick a soldier's pocket at the Zuwayla gate, was caught, and had his right hand cut off. The woman, learning of it, takes him in, gives him back all his gold from a chest where she had kept it, writes her property over to him and dies within fifty days. He returns to his broker's story: this is why he eats with his left hand,. The Christian ends by saying this is stranger than the Hunchback's tale; the King answers that they will all be hanged, and Shahrazād falls silent at dawn. Verse is copied as printed. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-ʿishrūna
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-sixth and-the-twenty,
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-sixth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ التَّاجِرَ قَالَ لِلنَّصْرَانِيِّ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba al-tājira qāla li-al-naṣrāniyyi
sentences.l: She-said: It-reached-me, O-you the-king the-happy, that the-young-man the-merchant said to-the-Christian:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that the young merchant said to the Christian:

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ وَجَلَسْتُ لَمْ أَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَالصَّبِيَّةُ قَدْ أَقْبَلَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا تَاجٌ مُكَلَّلٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ وَهِيَ مُنَقَّشَةٌ مُكَتَّبَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu wa-jalastu lam ashʿur illā wa-al-ṣabiyyatu qad aqbalat wa-ʿalayhā tājun mukallalun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari wa-hiya munaqqashatun mukattabatun
sentences.l: And-when I-entered and-I-sat, I-was-not-aware except and-the-young-woman had approached, and-upon-her (was) a-crown crowned with-the-pearl and-the-jewel, and-she (was) ornamented, inscribed.
sentences.i: When I had entered and sat down, I knew nothing until the young woman came toward me, a crown on her head studded with pearls and jewels, and she herself adorned and embroidered with writing.
sentences.n: لَمْ أَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَ... is the idiom "I was not aware, but that...": something happens suddenly. The pair مُنَقَّشَةٌ مُكَتَّبَةٌ is not clear to me: "ornamented, inscribed" may describe her dress embroidered with lettering, or the crown; I read it of her.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي تَبَسَّمَتْ فِي وَجْهِي وَحَضَنَتْنِي وَوَضَعَتْنِي عَلَى صَدْرِهَا وَجَعَلَتْ فِيهَا عَلَى فَمِي وَجَعَلَتْ تَمُصُّ لِسَانِي وَأَنَا كَذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī tabassamat fī wajhī wa-ḥaḍanatnī wa-waḍaʿatnī ʿalā ṣadrihā wa-jaʿalat fīhā ʿalā famī wa-jaʿalat tamuṣṣu lisānī wa-anā kadhālika
sentences.l: And-when she-saw-me she-smiled in my-face, and-she-embraced-me and-she-put-me upon her-chest, and-she-set her-mouth upon my-mouth, and-she-began she-sucks my-tongue, and-I (was) likewise.
sentences.i: When she saw me she smiled in my face, took me in her arms and laid me against her breast; she set her mouth on mine and began to suck my tongue, and I did the same.
sentences.n: فِيهَا is printed where Classical has فَاهَا, "her mouth" (the accusative of فُو). I take it so, since it is followed by "upon my mouth"; read as "in it" it would make no sense. جَعَلَتْ with a present verb, جَعَلَتْ تَمُصُّ, means "she began to suck".

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ صَحِيحٌ أَتَيْتَ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: wa-qālat ṣaḥīḥun atayta ʿindī
sentences.l: And-she-said: True! You-came at-me.
sentences.i: And she said: Truly, you have come to me!
sentences.n: أَتَى عِنْدِي, "come at me", uses عِنْدَ "at, with" where Classical would say إِلَيَّ "to me"; it is ordinary colloquial speech.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَنَا عَبْدُكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā anā ʿabduki
sentences.l: And-I-said to-her: I (am) your-slave.
sentences.i: I said to her: I am your slave.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَهْلًا وَمَرْحَبًا وَاللَّهِ مِنْ يَوْمِ رَأَيْتُكَ مَا لَذَّلِي نَوْمٌ وَلَا هَنَى لِي طَعَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ahlan wa-marḥaban wa-Allāhi min yawmi raʾaytuka mā ladhdhalī nawmun wa-lā hanā lī ṭaʿāmun
sentences.l: And-she-said: Welcome! and-ample-room! and-by-God, from (the)-day I-saw-you, not was-sweet-to-me sleep and-not was-wholesome to-me food.
sentences.i: She said: Welcome, and a wide welcome! By God, since the day I saw you, sleep has had no sweetness for me and food no savour.
sentences.n: لَذَّلِي is printed as one word: لَذَّ لِي "was pleasant to me". هَنَى is written with a final yā for Classical هَنَأَ "to be wholesome, to agree with one" (a Middle Arabic spelling, hamza lost). Both clauses are the old lovers' complaint of sleeplessness and lost appetite.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ وَأَنَا كَذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu wa-anā kadhālika
sentences.l: And-I-said: And-I (am) likewise.
sentences.i: I said: And I, the same.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَلَسْنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ وَأَنَا مُطْرِقٌ بِرَأْسِي إِلَى الْأَرْضِ حَيَاءً
sentences.tr: thumma jalasnā nataḥaddathu wa-anā muṭriqun bi-raʾsī ilā al-arḍi ḥayāʾan
sentences.l: Then we-sat we-converse, and-I (was) lowering with-my-head to the-earth, out-of-modesty.
sentences.i: Then we sat and talked, while I kept my head bowed toward the ground out of shyness.
sentences.n: أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ is "to bow the head", the verb taking بِـ for the thing lowered.

sentences.t: فَمَا لَبِثْتُ إِلَّاقُدِّمَتْ لِي سُفْرَةٌ مِنْ أَفْخَرِ أَلْوَانِ الْأَطْعِمَةِ مِنْ سِكْبَاجَهْ وَقُرْبُوسٍ مَقْلِيٍّ مُنَزَّلٍ فِي عَسَلِ نَحْلٍ وَدَجَاجٍ مَحْشِيٍّ
sentences.tr: fa-mā labithtu illāquddimat lī sufratun min afkhari alwāni al-aṭʿimati min sikbājah wa-qurbūsin maqliyyin munazzalin fī ʿasali naḥlin wa-dajājin maḥshiyyin
sentences.l: And-not I-lingered except was-set-before for-me a-spread from the-most-splendid-of kinds-of the-foods: from a-sikbāj, and-a-qurbūs fried, soaked in honey-of bees, and-a-fowl stuffed.
sentences.i: I had not waited long before a spread was laid before me of the choicest dishes: a sikbāj stew, a fried qurbūs steeped in bees' honey, and a stuffed fowl.
sentences.n: إِلَّاقُدِّمَتْ is printed as one word, إِلَّا قُدِّمَتْ. After مَا لَبِثْتُ Classical would have أَنْ; the bare past tense after إِلَّا is the common loose Middle Arabic way of saying "hardly had I waited when". سِكْبَاجَهْ ends in ه where Classical writes ة; the dish is sikbāj, meat stewed in vinegar. قُرْبُوس is literally the pommel of a saddle; as a dish I take it to be a pommel-shaped cut or piece of meat, but I am not sure of the exact meaning.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْتُ وَإِيَّاهَا وَاكْتَفَيْنَا فَقَدَّ مَوَالِي الطَّشْتَ وَالْإِ بْرِبْقَ فَغَسَلْتُ يَدَيَّ ثُمَّ تَطَيَّبْنَا بِالْمَاوَرْدِ الْمُمَسَّكِ
sentences.tr: fa-akaltu wa-iyyāhā wa-iktafaynā fa-qadda mawālī al-ṭashta wa-al-i bribqa fa-ghasaltu yadayya thumma taṭayyabnā bi-al-māwardi al-mumassaki
sentences.l: And-I-ate, and-she-too, and-we-had-enough; and-set-forth the-servants the-basin and-the-ewer; and-I-washed my-two-hands, then we-perfumed-ourselves with-the-rose-water the-musk-scented.
sentences.i: I ate, and she with me, until we had had enough. Then the servants brought the basin and the ewer, and I washed my hands, and afterwards we perfumed ourselves with musked rose-water.
sentences.n: This line is damaged in the print. فَقَدَّ مَوَالِي is printed as two words: I take it as فَقَدَّمَ مَوَالِي, "the servants brought", with one م lost where two met. وَالْإِ بْرِبْقَ is printed as two words and lacks the yā of إِبْرِيق, "ewer"; I point the letters as printed, which makes the pointing of the last two partly a guess at the sense. مَوَالِي, plural of مَوْلَى, here "servants, attendants" (not "masters"). مَاوَرْد is a contraction of مَاءُ وَرْدٍ, "rose-water".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَلَسْنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ فَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْ—يَ—اتِ
sentences.tr: thumma jalasnā nataḥaddathu fa-anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-ab—ya—āti
sentences.l: Then we-sat we-converse, and-she-recited, she-saying these the-ve—r—ses:
sentences.i: Then we sat and talked again, and she recited these verses:
sentences.n: الْأَبْ—يَ—اتِ is the compositor's broken printing of الْأَبْيَات, "the verses"; the dashes are printed, and I point the letters around them. Note that the verb is feminine: it is she who recites.

sentences.t:
لَوْ عَلِمْنَا قُدُومَكُمْ لَنَشَرْنَا * مُهْجَةَ الْقَلْبِ مَعَ سَوَادِ الْعُيُونُ
وَفَرَشْنَا خُدُودَنَا لِلِقَاكُمْ * لِيَكُونَ الْمَسِيرُ فَوْقَ الْجُفُونُ
sentences.tr:
law ʿalimnā qudūmakum la-nasharnā * muhjata al-qalbi maʿa sawādi al-ʿuyūnu
wa-farashnā khudūdanā li-liqākum * li-yakūna al-masīru fawqa al-jufūnu
sentences.l:
If we-had-known your-coming, we-would-have-scattered * the-heart's-lifeblood with the-blackness-of the-eyes,
and-we-would-have-spread our-cheeks for-your-meeting, * so-that-would-be the-walking above the-eyelids.
sentences.i: Had we known you were coming, we would have strewn before you the lifeblood of our hearts and the darkness of our eyes, and spread our cheeks out for your meeting, so that your walking might pass over our eyelids.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and copied as printed. The final nūn of الْعُيُونُ and الْجُفُونُ is printed with ḍamma, not the kasra a grammarian would give after مَعَ and فَوْقَ; it is the same ḍamma at the rhyme in both lines and I leave it. لِلِقَاكُمْ is a short form of لِلِقَائِكُمْ. The conceits are the lover's stock: a host who would give his heart's blood, the pupils of his eyes, even his cheeks as a carpet, so that the guest may walk on his eyelids.

sentences.t: وَهِيَ تَشْكُو إِلَيَّ مَالَاقَتْ وَأَنَا أَشْكُولَهَا مَالَا قَيْتُ وَتَمَكَّنَ حُبُّهَا عِنْدِي وَهَانَ عَلَيَّ جَمِيعُ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-hiya tashkū ilayya mālāqat wa-anā ashkūlahā mālā qaytu wa-tamakkana ḥubbuhā ʿindī wa-hāna ʿalayya jamīʿu al-māli
sentences.l: And-she complains to-me (of) what-she-met, and-I complain-to-her (of) what I-met; and-became-firm her-love with-me, and-became-easy upon-me all the-wealth.
sentences.i: She poured out to me what she had suffered, and I poured out to her what I had suffered. Her love took firm hold in me, and all my wealth seemed a light thing.
sentences.n: مَالَاقَتْ is one printed word, مَا لَاقَتْ; the second time the print breaks it wrongly, مَالَا قَيْتُ for مَا لَاقَيْتُ, with the yā lost. In the glossary the two pieces مَالَا and قَيْتُ are explained as fragments of that clause. وَهَانَ عَلَيَّ جَمِيعُ الْمَالِ is "all the money became light to me", that is, no longer mattered.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذْنَا نَلْعَبُ وَنَتَهَارَشُ وَنَتَبَاوَسُ إِلَى أَنْ أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadhnā nalʿabu wa-natahārashu wa-natabāwasu ilā an aqbala al-laylu
sentences.l: Then we-took we-play and-we-scratch-one-another and-we-kiss-one-another until that approached the-night.
sentences.i: Then we fell to playing, tussling and kissing each other until night came on.
sentences.n: نَتَبَاوَسُ, "we kiss one another", is built on the colloquial بَاسَ, "to kiss"; Classical would use نَتَقَابَلُ or نَتَقَبَّلُ. نَتَهَارَشُ is the mutual form of هَرَشَ, "to scratch", said of lovers' rough play.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمُوا لَنَا الْجَوَارِ الطَّعَامَ وَالْمُدَامَ فَإِذَا هِيَ حَضْرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddamū lanā al-jawāri al-ṭaʿāma wa-al-mudāma fa-idhā hiya ḥaḍratun kāmilatun
sentences.l: And-they-set-forth to-us the-slave-girls the-food and-the-wine, and-behold it (was) a-presence complete.
sentences.i: The slave girls set food and wine before us, and behold, it was a perfect gathering.
sentences.n: الْجَوَارِ is the plural of جَارِيَة, "slave girl", printed without its final yā (Classical الْجَوَارِي). The verb قَدَّمُوا is masculine plural with the subject added after it, where Classical would say قَدَّمَتِ الْجَوَارِي: colloquially, "they served us, the slave girls". حَضْرَةٌ is a "presence", a company or session, here a drinking-party.

sentences.t: فَشَرِبْنَا إِلَى نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ اضْطَجَعْنَا وَنِمْنَا فَنِمْتُ مَعَهَا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-sharibnā ilā niṣfi al-layli thumma iḍṭajaʿnā wa-nimnā fa-nimtu maʿahā ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And-we-drank until (the)-half-of the-night, then we-lay-down and-we-slept; and-I-slept with-her until the-morning.
sentences.i: We drank until the middle of the night, then lay down and slept, and I slept beside her until morning.

sentences.t: فَمَارَأَيْتُ عُمْرِي مِثْلَ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā raʾaytu ʿumrī mithla hādhihi al-laylati
sentences.l: And-not I-saw my-life the-like-of this the-night.
sentences.i: In all my life I never saw the like of that night.
sentences.n: The edition prints فَمَارَأَيْتُ as one word, with مَا glued to the verb; I keep it so. عُمْرِي is an accusative of time: "my life" for "in my life".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ قُمْتُ وَرَمَيْتُ لَهَا تَحْتَ الْفَرْشِ الْمِنْدِيلَ الَّذِي فِيهِ الدَّنَانِيرُ وَدَّعْتُهَا وَخَرَجْتُ فَبَكَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu qumtu wa-ramaytu lahā taḥta al-farshi al-mindīla alladhī fīhi al-danānīru wa-waddaʿtuhā wa-kharajtu fa-bakat
sentences.l: And-when became-morning the-morning, I-rose and-I-threw for-her under the-bedding the-handkerchief which in-it the-dinars, and-I-bade-her-farewell and-I-went-out, and-she-wept.
sentences.i: When morning came I got up and tossed down for her, beneath the bedding, the handkerchief with the dinars in it. I bade her farewell and went out, and she wept.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ, "the morning became morning", is the stock way of saying that day broke. The speaker pays the girl each night by leaving the knotted handkerchief of gold under her bedding.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي مَتَى أَرَى هَذَا الْوَجْهَ الْحَسَنَ فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَكُونُ عِنْدَكِ الْعَشَاءَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat yā sayyidī matā arā hādhā al-wajha al-ḥasana fa-qultu lahā akūnu ʿindaki al-ʿashāʾa
sentences.l: And-she-said: O my-master, when shall-I-see this the-face the-beautiful? And-I-said to-her: I-shall-be with-you (at) the-supper.
sentences.i: She said: My lord, when shall I see that lovely face again? I told her: I will be with you at suppertime.
sentences.n: عِنْدَكِ الْعَشَاءَ, "with you at supper", puts the time word in the accusative with no preposition. The print does not say whether it means العَشَاء, "supper", or العِشَاء, "the evening"; either way the promise is the same.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَرَجْتُ أَصَبْتُ الْحِمَارَ الَّذِي جَابَنِي بِالْأَمْسِ عَلَى الْبَابِ يَنْتَظِرُنِي فَرَكِبْتُ مَعَهُ حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ خَانَ مَسْرُورٍ فَنَزَلْتُ وَأَعْطَيْتُ الْحِمَارَ نِصْفَ دِينَارٍ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ تَعَالَ وَقْتَ الْغُرُوبِ قَالَ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kharajtu aṣabtu al-ḥimāra alladhī jābanī bi-al-amsi ʿalā al-bābi yantaẓirunī fa-rakibtu maʿahu ḥattā waṣaltu khāna Masrūrin fa-nazaltu wa-aʿṭaytu al-ḥimāra niṣfa dīnārin wa-qultu lahu taʿāla waqta al-ghurūbi qāla naʿam
sentences.l: And-when I-went-out I-hit-upon the-donkey which he-brought-me with-the-yesterday, at the-door, waiting-for-me. And-I-rode with-him until I-reached the-khan-of Masrur, and-I-dismounted, and-I-gave the-donkey half-of a-dinar, and-I-said to-him: Come (at the-)time-of the-sunset. He-said: Yes.
sentences.i: When I went out I found the donkey that had carried me the day before, waiting for me at the door, and I rode with its owner until we reached Masrur's Khan. There I dismounted, gave the donkey-man half a dinar, and said to him: Come at sunset. He said: Yes.
sentences.n: جَابَنِي, "he brought me", is the colloquial contraction of جَاءَ بِي; it is a Middle Arabic form and will recur. الْحِمَار stands for the donkey and its driver together: the one who answers "yes" at the end is the man. خَانُ مَسْرُورٍ is a merchants' inn named after a Masrur; the name is a personal name here.

sentences.t: فَفَطَرْتُ وَخَرَجْتُ أُطَالِبُ بِثَمَنِ الْقُمَاشِ ثُمَّ رَجَعْتُ وَقَدْ عَمِلْتُ لَهَا خَرُوفًا مَشْوِيًّا وَأَخَذْتُ حَلَاوَةً ثُمَّ دَعَوْتُ الْحَمَّالَ وَوَضَعْتُهُ لَهُ فِى الْمَحْمَلِ وَأَعْطَيْتُهُ أُجْرَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-faṭartu wa-kharajtu uṭālibu bi-thamani al-qumāshi thumma rajaʿtu wa-qad ʿamiltu lahā kharūfan mashwiyyan wa-akhadhtu ḥalāwatan thumma daʿawtu al-ḥammāla wa-waḍaʿtuhu lahu fī al-maḥmali wa-aʿṭaytuhu ujratahu
sentences.l: And-I-breakfasted, and-I-went-out demanding-with the-price-of the-cloth. Then I-returned, and-already I-had-made for-her a-lamb roasted, and-I-took a-sweetmeat. Then I-called the-porter, and-I-put-it for-him in the-carrier, and-I-gave-him his-wage.
sentences.i: I breakfasted and went out to collect the price of the cloth. Then I came back, having had a roast lamb prepared for her, and I took some sweetmeats too. I called a porter, set it all in his carrying-frame, and paid him his wage.
sentences.n: أُطَالِبُ بِثَمَنِ is "I press for the price": طَالَبَ takes بِـ for the thing demanded, and the verb stands bare after خَرَجْتُ with no particle. الْمَحْمَل is usually a litter or a pilgrim's palanquin; for a porter it must be his carrying-frame or basket, which is my guess.

sentences.t: وَرَجَعْتُ فِي أَشْغَالِي إِلَى الْغُرُوبِ فَجَاءَنِي الْمُكَارِي وَقْتَ الْمَغْرِبِ فَأَخَذْتُ خَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا وَجَعَلْتُهُمْ فِي مِنْدِيلٍ وَدَخَلْتُ عِنْدَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-rajaʿtu fī ashghālī ilā al-ghurūbi fa-jāʾanī al-mukārī waqta al-maghribi fa-akhadhtu khamsīna dīnāran wa-jaʿaltuhum fī mindīlin wa-dakhaltu ʿindahum
sentences.l: And-I-returned in my-occupations until the-sunset, and-came-to-me the-muleteer (at the-)time-of the-sunset; and-I-took fifty dinars, and-I-put-them in a-handkerchief, and-I-entered at-them.
sentences.i: I went back to my business until sunset, and at dusk the donkey-man came to me. I took fifty dinars, tied them in a handkerchief, and went in to the women.
sentences.n: جَعَلْتُهُمْ, "I put them", refers to the dinars with the plural pronoun used for persons (Classical would use the feminine singular or plural). عِنْدَهُمْ, "with them", is the girl and her maids, whom the edition has not named in this stretch. الْمُكَارِي, the muleteer, is the donkey-driver again.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُهُمْ مَسَحُوا الرُّخَامَ وَجَلَوُا النُّحَاسَ وَعَمَّرُوا الْقَنَادِيلَ وَأَوْقَدُوا الشُّمُوعَ وَغَرَفُوا الطَّعَامَ وَرَوَّقُوا الشَّرَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtuhum masaḥū al-rukhāma wa-jalawū al-nuḥāsa wa-ʿammarū al-qanādīla wa-awqadū al-shumūʿa wa-gharafū al-ṭaʿāma wa-rawwaqū al-sharāba
sentences.l: And-I-found-them they-had-wiped the-marble, and-polished the-brass, and-filled the-lamps, and-lit the-candles, and-ladled the-food, and-clarified the-drink.
sentences.i: I found that they had wiped down the marble, scoured the brass, filled the lamps, lit the candles, ladled out the food and strained the wine.
sentences.n: A run of household verbs, each a past tense with no "had" in the Arabic; the English perfect is mine. عَمَّرَ الْقَنَادِيلَ is "to fill the lamps" with oil, and رَوَّقَ الشَّرَابَ "to clear" the drink by straining it. فَوَجَدْتُهُمْ مَسَحُوا has no أَنَّ; the verb simply follows as a circumstantial clause.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْنِي رَمَتْ يَدَيْهَا عَلَى رَقَبَتِي وَقَالَتْ أَوْحَشْتَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾatnī ramat yadayhā ʿalā raqabatī wa-qālat awḥashtanī
sentences.l: And-when she-saw-me, she-threw her-two-hands upon my-neck, and-she-said: You-made-me-desolate.
sentences.i: When she saw me she threw her arms about my neck and said: How I have missed you!
sentences.n: أَوْحَشْتَنِي, "you have made me desolate", is the ordinary way to say "I missed you": the place was lonely without you.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُدِّمَتِ الْمَوَائِدُ فَأَكَلْنَا حَتَّى اكْتَفَيْنَا وَشَالَتِ الْجَوَارِ الْمَائِدَةَ وَقَدَّمْنَ الْمُدَامَ فَلَمْ نَزَلْ نَشْرَبُ إِلَى نِصْفِ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma quddimati al-mawāʾidu fa-akalnā ḥattā iktafaynā wa-shālati al-jawāri al-māʾidata wa-qaddamna al-mudāma fa-lam nazal nashrabu ilā niṣfi al-layli
sentences.l: Then were-presented the-tables, and-we-ate until we-were-content; and-lifted the-slave-girls the-table, and-they-presented the-wine; and-we-did-not cease we-drink until the-half-of the-night.
sentences.i: Then the tables were laid, and we ate until we were full. The slave girls cleared the table and brought in the wine, and we kept drinking until midnight.
sentences.n: The print has قدمت with no vowels; I read it as a passive, قُدِّمَتِ الْمَوَائِدُ, because the tables follow with no one doing the serving. وَشَالَتْ is colloquial: شَالَ here is "to lift away", where Classical شَالَ means to rise. الْجَوَارِ is printed without the final yāʾ of الْجَوَارِي ("the slave-girls"), and I point it as printed, with a kasra and no ending. Note the feminine plural قَدَّمْنَ for the girls.

sentences.t: فَقُمْنَا إِلَى مَجْلِسِ النَّوْمِ فَنِمْنَا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ فَقُمْتُ وَنَاوَلْتُهَا الْخَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا عَلَى الْعَادَةِ وَخَرَجْتُ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا فَوَجَدْتُ الْحِمَارَ فَرَكِبْتُ إِلَى خَانٍ فَنِمْتُ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qumnā ilā majlisi al-nawmi fa-nimnā ilā al-ṣabāḥi fa-qumtu wa-nāwaltuhā al-khamsīna dīnāran ʿalā al-ʿādati wa-kharajtu min ʿindihā fa-wajadtu al-ḥimāra fa-rakibtu ilā khānin fa-nimtu sāʿatan
sentences.l: And-we-rose to the-sitting-place-of the-sleep, and-we-slept until the-morning; and-I-rose, and-I-handed-her the-fifty dinars according-to the-custom, and-I-went-out from at-her, and-I-found the-donkey, and-I-rode to a-khan, and-I-slept an-hour.
sentences.i: We rose and went to the bedchamber and slept until morning. Then I got up and handed her the fifty dinars as usual, left her, found the donkey, and rode to a khan, where I slept for an hour.
sentences.n: مَجْلِسُ النَّوْمِ, "the sitting-place of sleep", is the sleeping chamber. خَانٍ is printed without the article, so I point it as "a khan", though "the khan" (his own lodging) is what is meant.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُمْتُ جَهَّزْتُ الْعَشَاءَ فَعَمِلْتُ جَوْزًا وَلَوْزًا وَتَحْتَهُمْ رُزٌّ مُفَلْفَلٌ وَعَمِلْتُ قُلْقَاسًا مَقْلِيًّا وَأَخَذْتُ فَاكِهَةً وَنُقْلًا وَمَشْمُومًا وَأَرْسَلْتُهُمْ وَسِرْتُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَأَخَذْتُ خَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا فِي مِنْدِيلٍ
sentences.tr: thumma qumtu jahhaztu al-ʿashāʾa fa-ʿamiltu jawzan wa-lawzan wa-taḥtahum ruzzun mufalfalun wa-ʿamiltu qulqāsan maqliyyan wa-akhadhtu fākihatan wa-nuqlan wa-mashmūman wa-arsaltuhum wa-sirtu ilā al-bayti wa-akhadhtu khamsīna dīnāran fī mindīlin
sentences.l: Then I-rose, I-prepared the-supper: and-I-made walnuts and-almonds, and-under-them rice peppered; and-I-made taro fried; and-I-took fruit and-dessert-nuts and-scented-things, and-I-sent-them, and-I-went to the-house, and-I-took fifty dinars in a-handkerchief.
sentences.i: Then I got up and prepared the supper. I made a dish of walnuts and almonds with peppered rice beneath it, and fried taro; I took fruit, nuts and sweets and flowers for the scent, sent it all ahead, went home, and took fifty dinars in a handkerchief.
sentences.n: قُمْتُ جَهَّزْتُ, "I rose, I prepared", strings two verbs with no conjunction, a colloquial habit that recurs. جَوْزًا is doubtful: جَوْز is "walnuts" (and also "a pair"), so the dish may be walnuts and almonds as a stuffing or topping; the grammar gives no more. وَتَحْتَهُمْ رُزٌّ is a verbless clause whose plural pronoun points back to them. قُلْقَاس is taro, a root vegetable; نُقْل is the nuts and sweets served with wine; مَشْمُوم is things to smell, flowers and fragrant herbs.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجْتُ رَكِبْتُ مَعَ الْحِمَارِ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ إِلَى الْقَاعَةِ فَدَخَلْتُ فَأَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا وَنِمْنَا إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ وَقُمْتُ رَمَيْتُ لَهَا الْمِنْدِيلَ وَرَكِبْتُ إِلَى الْخَانِ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-kharajtu rakibtu maʿa al-ḥimāri ʿalā al-ʿādati ilā al-qāʿati fa-dakhaltu fa-akalnā wa-sharibnā wa-nimnā ilā al-ṣabāḥi wa-qumtu ramaytu lahā al-mindīla wa-rakibtu ilā al-khāni ʿalā al-ʿādati
sentences.l: And-I-went-out, I-rode with the-donkey according-to the-custom to the-hall, and-I-entered, and-we-ate and-drank and-slept until the-morning; and-I-rose, I-threw for-her the-handkerchief, and-I-rode to the-khan according-to the-custom.
sentences.i: I went out, rode with the donkey-man as usual to the hall, and went in. We ate and drank and slept till morning, and I got up, tossed her the handkerchief, and rode to the khan, as was my habit.
sentences.n: الْقَاعَة is the great hall of a house, here the girl's reception room. Again خَرَجْتُ رَكِبْتُ and قُمْتُ رَمَيْتُ run two verbs together without wa-.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَزَلْ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ مُدَّةً إِلَى أَنْ بِتُّ وَأَصْبَحْتُ لَا أَمْلِكُ دِرْهَمًا وَلَا دِينَارًا
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati muddatan ilā an bittu wa-aṣbaḥtu lā amliku dirhaman wa-lā dīnāran
sentences.l: And-I-did-not cease upon that the-state (for) a-while, until I-spent-the-night and-I-became-at-morning not owning a-dirham and-not a-dinar.
sentences.i: I went on in that way for a time, until I went to bed one night and woke the next day owning neither dirham nor dinar.
sentences.n: بِتُّ وَأَصْبَحْتُ, "I spent the night and rose at morning", is the usual pair for the passage of a night; here it carries the sudden turn: he is penniless between one evening and the next dawn.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي كُلُّ هَذَا مِنْ فِعْلِ الشَّيْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu fī nafsī kullu hādhā min fiʿli al-shayṭāni
sentences.l: And-I-said in my-self: All (of) this (is) from the-doing-of the-devil.
sentences.i: I said to myself: All this is the work of Satan.
sentences.n: This echoes the Qurʾānic "this is of Satan's work" (28:15), though the print has فِعْل, "doing", where the Qurʾān has عَمَل.

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْ—يَ—اتِ
sentences.tr: wa-anshadtu aqūlu hādhihi al-ab—ya—āti
sentences.l: And-I-recited, I-say these the-verses.
sentences.i: And I recited, saying these verses:
sentences.n: The print breaks the word الأبيات, "the verses", with dashes inside it; I keep them as printed and point the letters around them.

sentences.t:
فَقْرُ الْغَنِىّ يُذْهِبُ اَنْوَارَهُ * كَمَا اصْفِرَارُ الشَّمْسِ عِنْدَ الْمَغِيبِ
اِنْ غَابَ لَايُذْكَرُ بَيْنَ الْوَرَى * وَاِنْ حَضَرَ فِى الْحَيِّ مَالَهُ نَصِيبِ
يَمْشِي فِى الْاَسْوَاقِ مُسْتَخْفِيًا * وَفِى الْفَلَا يَبْكِي بِدَمْعٍ صَبِيبِ
وَاللهِ مَا الْاِنْسَانُ بَيْنَ اَهْلِهِ * اِذَا بُلِي بِالْفَقْرِ اِلَّا غَرِيبِ
sentences.tr:
faqru al-ghaniyyi yudhhibu anwārahu * kamā iṣfirāru al-shamsi ʿinda al-maghībi
in ghāba lā yudhkaru bayna al-warā * wa-in ḥaḍara fī al-ḥayyi mā lahu naṣībi
yamshī fī al-aswāqi mustakhfiyan * wa-fī al-falā yabkī bi-damʿin ṣabībi
wa-Allāhi mā al-insānu bayna ahlihi * idhā buliya bi-al-faqri illā gharībi
sentences.l:
The-poverty-of the-rich-man removes his-lights, * just-as the-yellowing-of the-sun at the-setting.
If he-is-absent, not he-is-mentioned among the-mankind; * and-if he-is-present in the-quarter, not to-him (is) a-share.
He-walks in the-markets hiding-himself, * and-in the-wilderness he-weeps with-a-tear pouring.
And-by-God, not (is) the-human among his-kin, * when he-is-afflicted with-the-poverty, except a-stranger.
sentences.i: The poverty of one who was rich puts out his lights, as the sun yellows at its setting. If he is away, no one speaks of him among the people; if he is in the quarter, he has no standing. He walks the markets in hiding, and in the wild places he weeps with streaming tears. By God, a man among his own kin, once poverty has struck him, is nothing but a stranger.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed. Every line ends in a printed kasra on the rhyme word (الْمَغِيبِ، نَصِيبِ، صَبِيبِ، غَرِيبِ), even where Classical grammar would want another vowel (نَصِيبٌ and غَرِيبٌ would be nominative); I keep what is printed. كَمَا اصْفِرَارُ الشَّمْسِ has no verb: "just as the yellowing of the sun". أَنْوَارُهُ, "his lights", is his radiance, his good name and standing. فِي الْحَيِّ is "in the quarter", among his own neighbours. لَايُذْكَرُ is printed with the negative glued to the verb.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ الْخَانِ وَمَشَيْتُ بَيْنَ الْقَصْرَيْنِ وَلَا زِلْتُ أمْشِي إلَى بَابِ زُوَيْلَةَ فَوَجَدْتُ الْخَلْقَ فِي ازْدِحَامٍ وَالْبَابُ مَسْدُودٌ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الْخَلْقِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajtu mina al-khāni wa-mashaytu bayna al-qaṣrayni wa-lā ziltu amshī ilā bābi Zuwaylata fa-wajadtu al-khalqa fī izdiḥāmin wa-al-bābu masdūdun min kathrati al-khalqi
sentences.l: And-I-went-out from the-khan, and-I-walked between the-two-palaces, and-I-did-not-cease walking to the-gate-of Zuwayla; and-I-found the-creation in crowding, and-the-gate blocked from abundance-of the-creation.
sentences.i: I left the khan and walked between the Two Palaces, and went on walking until I came to the Zuwayla Gate. There I found the people in a dense throng, and the gate stopped up by the sheer number of them.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ الْقَصْرَيْنِ: the 'Two Palaces', the well-known street of Cairo (Bayn al-Qaṣrayn). الْخَلْقَ, literally 'the creation', is the ordinary word here for 'the people, the crowd'.

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ بِالْأمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ جُنْدِىًّ فَزَاحَمْتُهُ بِغَيْرِ اخْتِيَارِى فَجَاءَتْ يَدِي عَلَى جَيْبِهِ فَحَسَيْتُ فَوَجَدْتُ صُرَّةً مِنْ دَاخِلِ الْجَيْبِ الَّذِي يَدِي عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu bi-al-amri al-muqaddari jundiyyan fa-zāḥamtuhu bi-ghayri ikhtiyārī fa-jāʾat yadī ʿalā jaybihi fa-ḥasaytu fa-wajadtu ṣurratan min dākhili al-jaybi alladhī yadī ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-I-saw by-the-command the-decreed a-soldier, and-I-jostled-him without choice-of-mine, and-came my-hand upon his-pocket, and-I-felt, and-I-found a-purse from inside-of the-pocket which my-hand [was] upon-it.
sentences.i: By the decree of fate I caught sight of a soldier and, quite against my will, jostled him; my hand came down on his pocket, and feeling about I found a purse inside the very pocket where my hand lay.
sentences.n: جُنْدِىًّ: the print writes the accusative without its alif, with final ى; we read it as an accusative, 'a soldier'. فَحَسَيْتُ: Middle Arabic for Classical حَسَسْتُ, 'I felt', with the doubled radical replaced by a glide.

sentences.t: فَعَلِمْتُ إنَّهَا مُتَّصِلَةٌ بِتِلْكَ الصُّرَّةِ فَأخَذْتُهَا مِنْ جَيْبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿalimtu annahā muttaṣilatun bi-tilka al-ṣurrati fa-akhadhtuhā min jaybihi
sentences.l: And-I-knew that-it [was] joined to that purse, and-I-took-it from his-pocket.
sentences.i: I understood it to be tied to that very purse, and I took it from his pocket.
sentences.n: مُتَّصِلَةٌ بِتِلْكَ الصُّرَّةِ, 'joined to that purse', is obscure: the sense seems to be that what the hand found was the purse itself, attached within the pocket. We translate what is printed and do not repair it.

sentences.t: فَحَسَّ الْجُنْدِيُّ بِأنَّ جَيْبَهُ خَفَّ فَحَطَّ يَدَهُ فِي جَيْبِهِ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ شَيْئًا وَالْتَفَتَ نَحْوِي وَشَالَ يَدَهُ بِاللَّ بُّوسِ وَضَرَبَنِي عَلَى رَأْسِي فَسَقَطْتُ إلَى الْأرْضِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥassa al-jundiyyu bi-anna jaybahu khaffa fa-ḥaṭṭa yadahu fī jaybihi fa-lam yajid shayʾan wa-iltafata naḥwī wa-shāla yadahu bi-al-labbūsi wa-ḍarabanī ʿalā raʾsī fa-saqaṭtu ilā al-arḍi
sentences.l: And-felt the-soldier that his-pocket had-grown-light, and-put his-hand in his-pocket and-did-not find a-thing; and-he-turned toward-me, and-raised his-hand with-the-club, and-struck-me on my-head, and-I-fell to the-ground.
sentences.i: The soldier sensed that his pocket had grown light; he thrust his hand into it and found nothing. Then he turned on me, lifted his hand with his cudgel, and struck me on the head, so that I fell to the ground.
sentences.n: بِاللَّ بُّوسِ: the print splits the word; it is al-labbūs, a club or cudgel, read as one word. فَحَطَّ and وَشَالَ are colloquial verbs ('put', 'lifted').

sentences.t: فَأحَاطُوا بِنَا النَّاسُ وَمَسَكُوا لِجَامَ فَرَسِ الْجُنْدِيِّ وَقَالُوا لِأجْلِ الزَّحْمَةِ تَضْرِبُ هَذَا الشَّابَّ هَذِهِ الضَّرْبَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-aḥāṭū bi-nā al-nāsu wa-masakū lijāma farasi al-jundiyyi wa-qālū li-ajli al-zaḥmati taḍribu hādhā al-shābba hādhihi al-ḍarbata
sentences.l: And-surrounded us the-people, and-gripped the-bridle-of the-horse-of the-soldier, and-said: for-the-sake-of the-crush you-strike this the-youth this the-blow?
sentences.i: The people crowded around us and seized the bridle of the soldier's horse. 'For a little jostling,' they said, 'you strike this young man such a blow?'
sentences.n: فَا@حَاطُوا ... النَّاسُ: the plural verb precedes its subject, a Middle Arabic habit (Classical would say أَحَاطَ بِنَا النَّاسُ). وَمَسَكُوا, 'they gripped', is the colloquial verb for Classical أَمْسَكُوا.

sentences.t: فَصَرَخَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْجُنْدِيُّ وَقَالَ هَذَا حَرَامِيٌّ مَلْعُونٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣarakha ʿalayhimu al-jundiyyu wa-qāla hādhā ḥarāmiyyun malʿūnun
sentences.l: And-shouted at-them the-soldier and-said: This [is] a-thief, accursed!
sentences.i: The soldier shouted back at them, 'This is a thief, a cursed one!'
sentences.n: حَرَامِيٌّ is the colloquial word for 'thief' (literally 'a forbidden-doer, a robber').

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اسْتَفَقْتُ وَرَأَيْتُ النَّاسَ يَقُولُونَ هَذَا شَابٌّ مَلِيحٌ لَمْ يَأْخُذْ شَيْئًا فَبَعْضُهُمْ يُصَدِّقُ وَبَعْضُهُمْ يُكَذِّبُ وَكَثُرَ الْقَالُ وَالْقِيلُ وَ جَذَبُونِي النَّاسُ وَأرَادُواخَلَاصِي مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika istafaqtu wa-raʾaytu al-nāsa yaqūlūna hādhā shābbun malīḥun lam yaʾkhudh shayʾan fa-baʿḍuhum yuṣaddiqu wa-baʿḍuhum yukadhdhibu wa-kathura al-qālu wa-al-qīlu wa jadhabūnī al-nāsu wa-arādū khalāṣī minhu
sentences.l: And-at that I-came-to, and-I-saw the-people saying: This [is] a-youth handsome, he-did-not take a-thing; and-some-of-them believes and-some-of-them calls-a-liar; and-abounded the-said-and the-it-is-said; and they-pulled-me, the-people, and-they-wanted my-deliverance from-him.
sentences.i: Then I came to my senses and saw the people saying, 'This is a handsome young man; he has taken nothing.' Some believed it and some did not, and there was talk and counter-talk, and the people pulled me away, wishing to free me from him.
sentences.n: الْقَالُ وَالْقِيلُ, 'the said and the it-is-said', is an idiom for gossip and disputing. The print has a stray وَ at the end of its line and then جَذَبُونِي النَّاسُ, again a plural verb before its subject; and it runs وَا@رَادُواخَلَاصِي together as one word (read: and they wanted my deliverance).

sentences.t: فَبِا لْأمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ وَإذَا بِالْوَالِي وَالْمُقَدَّمِ وَالظَّلَمَةِ دَخَلُوا مِنَ الْبَابِ فَوَجَدُوا الْخَلْقَ مُجْتَمِعِينَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى الْجُنْدِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-bi-ā al-amri al-muqaddari wa-idhā bi-al-wālī wa-al-muqaddami wa-al-ẓalamati dakhalū mina al-bābi fa-wajadū al-khalqa mujtamiʿīna ʿalayya wa-ʿalā al-jundiyyi
sentences.l: And-by the-command the-decreed, and-behold, the-governor and-the-captain and-the-oppressors [officers] entered from the-gate, and-found the-creation gathered upon-me and-upon the-soldier.
sentences.i: And by that same decree, in came the governor with his captain and his men through the gate, and found the crowd gathered around me and the soldier.
sentences.n: فَبِا لْا@مْرِ: the print splits the word after the alif; it is simply فَبِالْأَمْرِ. بِالْوَالِي after وَإِذَا: the بِـ only marks what appears ('and behold, the governor'). الظَّلَمَةُ, literally 'the wrongdoers', is the common name for a governor's officers and bailiffs.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَالِي مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wālī mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: And-said the-governor: What [is] the-news?
sentences.i: The governor said, 'What is the matter?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْجُنْدِيُّ وَاللَّهِ يَا خَوَنْدُ هَذَا حَرَامِيٌّ وَكَانَ فِي جَيْبِي كِيسٌ أزْرَقُ فِيهِ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا فَأخَذَهُ وَأنَا فِىَ الزِّحَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-jundiyyu wa-Allāhi yā khawandu hādhā ḥarāmiyyun wa-kāna fī jaybī kīsun azraqu fīhi ʿishrūna dīnāran fa-akhadhahu wa-anā fī al-ziḥāmi
sentences.l: And-said the-soldier: By-God, O khawand, this [is] a-thief! And-there-was in my-pocket a-purse blue, in-it twenty dinars, and-he-took-it while-I [was] in the-crush.
sentences.i: 'By God, my lord,' said the soldier, 'this man is a thief! I had a blue purse in my pocket with twenty dinars in it, and he took it while I was in the crush.'
sentences.n: خَوَنْدُ (Persian-Turkish khwand, khawand) is a title of respect, 'lord, master', used to a high official.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَالِي لِلْجُنْدِيِّ هَلْ كَانَ مَعَكَ أحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wālī li-al-jundiyyi hal kāna maʿaka aḥadun
sentences.l: And-said the-governor to-the-soldier: Was with-you anyone?
sentences.i: The governor said to the soldier, 'Was anyone with you?'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْجُنْدِيُّ لَافَصَرَخَ الْوَالِي عَلَى الْمُقَدَّمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-jundiyyu lā-fa-ṣarakha al-wālī ʿalā al-muqaddami
sentences.l: And-said the-soldier: No. And-shouted the-governor at the-captain,
sentences.i: 'No,' said the soldier. The governor cried out to his captain,
sentences.n: لَافَصَرَخَ: the print runs لَا and فَصَرَخَ together as one word; read 'No' and 'and he cried out'.

sentences.t: فَمَسَكَنِي وَقَدْ زَالَ السِّتْرُ عَنِّي فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَالِي عَرِّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-masakanī wa-qad zāla al-sitru ʿannī fa-qāla lahu al-wālī ʿarrihi
sentences.l: And-he-gripped-me, and-already had-gone the-covering from-me; and-said to-him the-governor: Strip-him!
sentences.i: who seized me, for my protection had been lifted from me. The governor said to him, 'Strip him!'
sentences.n: السِّتْرُ, 'the covering', is the concealing protection that had hitherto shielded the narrator; its departure marks the turn of his fortune.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَرَّوْنِي وَجَدُوا الْكِيسَ فِي ثِيَابِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿarrawnī wajadū al-kīsa fī thiyābī
sentences.l: And-when they-stripped-me, they-found the-purse in my-clothes.
sentences.i: When they stripped me, they found the purse in my clothes.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَجَدُوا الْكِيسَ أخَذَهُ الْوَالِي وَفَتَحَهُ وَعَدَّهُ فَرَأَى فِيهِ عِشْرِينَ دِينَارًا كَمَا قَالَ الْجُنْدِيُّ فَغَضِبَ الْوَالِي وَعَيَّطَ عَلَى الْمُقَدَّمِينَ فَقَدَّمُونِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā wajadū al-kīsa akhadhahu al-wālī wa-fataḥahu wa-ʿaddahu fa-raʾā fīhi ʿishrīna dīnāran kamā qāla al-jundiyyu fa-ghaḍiba al-wālī wa-ʿayyaṭa ʿalā al-muqaddamīna fa-qaddamūnī bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And-when they-found the-purse, took-it the-governor and-opened-it and-counted-it, and-saw in-it twenty dinars as said the-soldier; and-grew-angry the-governor, and-shouted at the-captains, and-they-presented-me between his-hands.
sentences.i: When they found the purse, the governor took it, opened it and counted: twenty dinars, just as the soldier had said. He fell into a rage, called out to his captains, and they brought me before him.
sentences.n: وَعَيَّطَ, 'he shouted', is a colloquial verb (Classical صَاحَ). بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, 'between his hands', is the idiom for 'in his presence'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي يَا صَبِيُّ قُلِ الْحَقَّ أنْتَ سَرَقْتَ هَذَا الْكِيسَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī yā ṣabiyyu quli al-ḥaqqa anta saraqta hādhā al-kīsa
sentences.l: And-he-said to-me: O boy, say the-truth: you stole this the-purse?
sentences.i: He said to me, 'Boy, tell the truth: did you steal this purse?'

sentences.t: فَأطْرَقْتُ بِرَأْسِي إلَى الْأرْضِ وَقُلْتُ أنَا إنْ قُلْتُ مَا سَرَقْتُ أخْرَجْتُهُ وَإنْ قُلْتُ سَرَقْتُهُ وَقَعْتُ فِىَ الْعَنَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraqtu bi-raʾsī ilā al-arḍi wa-qultu anā in qultu mā saraqtu akhrajtuhu wa-in qultu saraqtuhu waqaʿtu fī al-ʿanāʾi
sentences.l: And-I-lowered with-my-head to the-ground, and-I-said: I, if I-say 'I-did-not-steal', I-brought-it-out, and-if I-say 'I-stole-it', I-fell into the-hardship.
sentences.i: I lowered my head to the ground and said to myself: if I say I did not steal, the purse has already been brought out; and if I say I stole it, I fall into misery.
sentences.n: ا@خْرَجْتُهُ, 'I brought it out', is obscure: either the purse is already out of my clothes (so denial is futile) or 'I would have to produce it'; the dilemma is the same either way. We keep the past form the print gives.

sentences.t: فَشَلْتُ رَأْسِي فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ أخَذْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-shaltu raʾsī fa-qultu naʿam akhadhtuhu
sentences.l: And-I-lifted my-head and-I-said: Yes, I-took-it.
sentences.i: I lifted my head and said, 'Yes, I took it.'

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ مِنِّي الْوَالِي هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَعَجَّبَ وَدَعَا بِالشُّهُودِ فَحَضَرُوا وَشَهِدُوا عَلَى مَنْطِقِي هَذَا كُلِّهِ فِي بَابِ زُوَيْلَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa minnī al-wālī hādhā al-kalāma taʿajjaba wa-daʿā bi-al-shuhūdi fa-ḥaḍarū wa-shahidū ʿalā manṭiqī hādhā kullihi fī bābi Zuwaylata
sentences.l: And-when heard from-me the-governor this the-speech, he-marvelled, and-called for the-witnesses; and-they-attended and-testified upon my-speech this all-of-it in the-gate-of Zuwayla.
sentences.i: When the governor heard these words from me he marvelled, and sent for witnesses; they came and bore witness to this whole avowal of mine at the Zuwayla Gate.
sentences.n: دَعَا بِـ, 'he called for', takes the thing summoned with بِـ.

sentences.t: فَأمَرَ الْوَالِي الْمَشَا عِلِىَّ فَقَطَعَ يَدِىَ الْيَمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-wālī al-mashā ʿiliyya fa-qaṭaʿa yadiya al-yamīna
sentences.l: And-commanded the-governor the-torch-bearer [executioner], and-he-cut my-hand the-right.
sentences.i: The governor ordered the executioner, who cut off my right hand.
sentences.n: الْمَشَا عِلِىَّ: the print splits the word; it is al-mashāʿilī, the 'torch-bearer' (from mashʿal), the officer who carried out sentences. The accusative is ours; the print has only the bare letters.

sentences.t: فَرَقَّ قَلْبُ الْجُنْدِيِّ فَشَفَعَ فِيَّ وَتَرَكَنِي الْوَالِي وَمَضَى وَبَقِيَتِ النَّاسُ حَوْلِي وَسَقَوْنِي قَدَحَ شَرَابٍ
sentences.tr: fa-raqqa qalbu al-jundiyyi fa-shafaʿa fiyya wa-tarakanī al-wālī wa-maḍā wa-baqiyati al-nāsu ḥawlī wa-saqawnī qadaḥa sharābin
sentences.l: And-softened the-heart-of the-soldier, and-he-interceded for-me; and-left-me the-governor and-went-off; and-remained the-people around-me, and-they-gave-me-to-drink a-cup-of drink.
sentences.i: The soldier's heart softened and he interceded for me; the governor left me and went on his way. The people stayed about me and gave me a cup of drink.

sentences.t: وَأمَّا الْجُنْدِىُّ فَإنَّهُ أعْطَانِي الْكِيسَ وَقَالَ أنْتَ شَابٌّ مَلِيحٌ وَلَا يَنْبَغِي أنْ تَكُونَ لِصًّا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-jundiyyu fa-innahu aʿṭānī al-kīsa wa-qāla anta shābbun malīḥun wa-lā yanbaghī an takūna liṣṣan
sentences.l: And-as-for the-soldier, then-indeed-he gave-me the-purse and-said: You [are] a-youth handsome, and-not it-is-fitting that you-be a-thief.
sentences.i: As for the soldier, he gave me the purse and said, 'You are a handsome young man, and it does not befit you to be a thief.'

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إنِّي أنْشَدْتُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: thumma innī anshadtu shiʿran
sentences.l: Then indeed-I recited poetry.
sentences.i: Then I recited some verses.
sentences.n: The verses follow in the next unit.

sentences.t:
وَاللّٰهِ مَاكُنْتُ لِصًّا يَا اَخَاثِقَةِ * وَلَا اَنَا سَارِقٌ يَا اَحْسَنَ النَّاسِ
لَكِنْ رَمَتْنِي صُرُوفُ الدَّهْرِ عَنْ عَجَلٍ * فَزَادَ هَمِّي وَوَسْوَاسِي وَافْلَاسِي
وَمَا رَمَيْتَ وَلَكِنَّ الاِلَهَ رَمَى * سَهْمًا فَطَيَّرَ تَاجَ الْمُلْكِ عَنْ رَأْسِي
sentences.tr:
wa-Allāhi mā kuntu liṣṣan yā akhā thiqatin * wa-lā anā sāriqun yā aḥsana al-nāsi
lākin ramatnī ṣurūfu al-dahri ʿan ʿajalin * fa-zāda hammī wa-waswāsī wa-iflāsī
wa-mā ramayta wa-lākinna al-ilāha ramā * sahman fa-ṭayyara tāja al-mulki ʿan raʾsī
sentences.l:
By-God, I-was-not a-thief, O brother-of-trust, * and-not I a-stealer, O best-of the-people.
But shot-me the-turns-of the-time in haste, * so-increased my-care and-my-whisperings and-my-penury.
And-you-did-not shoot, but the-Deity shot, * an-arrow, and-sent-flying the-crown-of the-kingship from my-head.
sentences.i: By God, I was no thief, O man of trust, nor am I a robber, best of men. But the blows of fate struck me down in haste, and so my care grew, and my fears, and my beggary. It was not you who shot; it was God who shot an arrow, and it sent the crown of kingship flying from my head.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed. اَخَاثِقَةِ is أَخَا ثِقَةٍ "brother of trust" (a trustworthy man) run together, and the printed مَاكُنْتُ likewise runs مَا كُنْتُ together. The last line plays on the Qur'anic وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَى (8:17): the speaker says that it was not the man who struck him but God, whose arrow of fortune knocked the crown from his head. الاِلَهَ "the Deity" is printed with the article's alif unpointed, as the print has it. وَافْلَاسِي is printed without hamza; "my penury" shows that the speaker is a king fallen to beggary.

sentences.t: فَتَرَكَنِي الْجُنْدِيُّ وَانْصَرَفَ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَعْطَانِي الْكِيسَ وَانْصَرَفْتُ أَنَا وَلَفَفْتُ يَدِي فِي خِرْقَةٍ وَأَدْخَلْتُهَا عُبِّي وَقَدْ تَغَيَّرَتْ حَالَتِي وَاصْفَرَّلَوْنِي مِمَّا جَرَى عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-tarakanī al-jundiyyu wa-inṣarafa baʿda an aʿṭānī al-kīsa wa-inṣaraftu anā wa-lafaftu yadī fī khirqatin wa-adkhaltuhā ʿubbī wa-qad taghayyarat ḥālatī wa-iṣfarra lawnī mimmā jarā ʿalayya
sentences.l: And-left-me the-soldier, and-departed after that he-gave-me the-purse; and-departed-I, I; and-I-wrapped my-hand in a-rag and-I-put-it-in my-bosom; and-had changed my-state, and-went-yellow-my-colour from-what happened upon-me.
sentences.i: So the soldier let me go and went his way, after handing me the purse; and I too went off, wrapped my hand in a rag and tucked it into my bosom. My whole state was altered, and my colour had turned sallow from all that had befallen me.
sentences.n: وَاصْفَرَّلَوْنِي is two words run together, وَاصْفَرَّ لَوْنِي, "and my colour turned yellow". عُبِّي is the fold of the garment at the breast, where one tucks things.

sentences.t: فَتَمَشَّيْتُ إِلَى الْقَاعَةِ وَأَنَا عَلَى غَيْرِ اسْتِوَاءٍ وَرَمَيْتُ رُوحِي عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ
sentences.tr: fa-tamashshaytu ilā al-qāʿati wa-anā ʿalā ghayri istiwāʾin wa-ramaytu rūḥī ʿalā al-firāshi
sentences.l: And-I-walked-slowly to the-hall, and-I upon other-than evenness; and-I-threw my-spirit upon the-bed.
sentences.i: I made my way to the hall, all unsteady, and flung myself down on the bed.
sentences.n: عَلَى غَيْرِ اسْتِوَاءٍ is "not on an even keel", out of sorts. رَمَى رُوحَهُ "throw one's spirit" is the colloquial way of saying "throw oneself"; the Middle Arabic uses رُوح for the self.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَتْنِي الصَّبِيَّةُ مُتَغَيِّرًا اللَّوْنَ فَقَالَتْ لِي مَا وَجَعُكَ وَمَالِي أَرَى حَالَتَكَ تَغَيَّرَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓaratnī al-ṣabiyyatu mutaghayyiran al-lawna fa-qālat lī mā wajaʿuka wa-mālī arā ḥālataka taghayyarat
sentences.l: And-looked-at-me the-young-woman, changed(acc.) the-colour(acc.); and-she-said to-me: What (is) your-pain, and-what-(is)-to-me, I-see your-state, it-has-changed?
sentences.i: The young woman looked at me and saw my colour altered, and said, "What ails you? Why do I see you in such a changed state?"
sentences.n: نَظَرَتْنِي "she looked at me" takes a direct object where Classical would have نَظَرَتْ إِلَيَّ. مُتَغَيِّرًا اللَّوْنَ is printed with the accusative ending on both words; I take it as a state with an accusative of respect, "changed as to colour" (Classical would more often say مُتَغَيِّرَ اللَّوْنِ).

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا رَأْسِي يُوجِعُنِي وَمَا أَنَا طَيِّبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā raʾsī yūjiʿunī wa-mā anā ṭayyibun
sentences.l: And-I-said to-her: My-head pains-me, and-not I well.
sentences.i: I told her, "My head pains me, and I am not well."
sentences.n: طَيِّب "well, in good health" is the everyday sense, the one the Middle Arabic uses; Classical would say صَحِيح or عَافِي.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ اغْتَاظَتْ وَتَشَوَّشَتْ لِأَجْلِي وَقَالَتْ لَاتُحْرِقْ قَلْبِي يَا سَيِّدِي اقْعُدْ وَشُلْ رَأْسَكَ وَحَدِّثْنِي بِمَا قَدْتَمَّ لَكَ الْيَوْمَ فَقَدْ بَانَ لِي فِي وَجْهِكَ كَلَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ightāẓat wa-tashawwashat li-ajlī wa-qālat lā tuḥriq qalbī yā sayyidī uqʿud wa-shul raʾsaka wa-ḥaddithnī bi-mā qad tamma laka al-yawma fa-qad bāna lī fī wajhika kalāmun
sentences.l: And-at that she-was-vexed and-was-disturbed for-my-sake, and-she-said: Do-not-burn my-heart, O my-master; sit, and-lift your-head, and-tell-me of-what has-befallen to-you the-day, for-has appeared to-me in your-face a-word.
sentences.i: At that she grew vexed and troubled on my account, and said, "Do not wound my heart, my lord. Sit up, lift your head, and tell me what has befallen you today, for I can read something in your face."
sentences.n: لَا تُحْرِقْ قَلْبِي "do not burn my heart" means "do not grieve me". شُلْ is the colloquial imperative of شَالَ, "lift" (Classical اِرْفَعْ). قَدْتَمَّ is قَدْ تَمَّ run together. بَانَ لِي فِي وَجْهِكَ كَلَامٌ is "there shows to me in your face something to be said", that is, your face tells of a story.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ دَعِينِي مِنَ الْكَلَامِ فَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ كَأَنَّكَ قَدْ فَرَغَ غَرَضُكَ مِنِّي فَإِنِّي أَرَاكَ بِخِلَافِ الْعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu daʿīnī mina al-kalāmi fa-bakat wa-qālat ka-annaka qad faragha gharaḍuka minnī fa-innī arāka bi-khilāfi al-ʿādati
sentences.l: And-I-said: Leave-me from the-talk. And-she-wept and-said: As-though-you, has finished your-purpose from-me; for-I I-see-you contrary-to the-custom.
sentences.i: "Spare me the talk," I said. She wept and said, "It seems you have had your fill of me, for I see you not as you are wont to be."
sentences.n: دَعِينِي مِنَ الْكَلَامِ is the colloquial "leave me out of talk", that is, "spare me". The verb is printed unpointed; I read فَرَغَ "was finished", so that her words mean "your purpose with me is spent".

sentences.t: فَسَكَتُّ وَصَارَتْ تُحَدِّثُنِي وَأَنَا لَا أُجِيبُهَا حَتَّى أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ
sentences.tr: fa-sakattu wa-ṣārat tuḥaddithunī wa-anā lā ujībuhā ḥattā aqbala al-laylu
sentences.l: And-I-fell-silent, and-she-became she-talks-to-me, and-I not I-answer-her until came-on the-night.
sentences.i: I fell silent, and she went on talking to me while I gave her no answer, until night came on.
sentences.n: صَارَتْ تُحَدِّثُنِي "she became (one who) talks to me", that is, she went on talking: صَارَ plus an imperfect marks a beginning or a continuing action.

sentences.t: فَقَدَّمَتْ لِي الطَّعَامَ فَامْتَنَعْتُ مِنْهُ وَخَشِيتُ أَنْ تَرَانِي آكُلُ بِيَدِي الشِّمَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaddamat lī al-ṭaʿāma fa-imtanaʿtu minhu wa-khashītu an tarānī ākulu bi-yadī al-shimāli
sentences.l: And-she-presented to-me the-food, and-I-refrained from-it, and-I-feared that she-sees-me eating with-my-hand the-left.
sentences.i: She set food before me, but I held back from it, for I feared she would see me eating with my left hand.
sentences.n: الشِّمَال "the left" as an adjective of يَد is the Middle Arabic way of saying "left hand" (Classical الْيُسْرَى or الشِّمَال as a noun).

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَاأَشْتَهِي أَنْ آكُلَ فِي هَذِةِ السَّاعَةِ فَقَالَتْ حَدِّثْنِي بِمَا تَمَّ لَكَ الْيَوْمَ وَمَالَكَ مَهْمُومٌ وَمَكْسُورُالْخَاطِرِ وَالْقَلْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā ashtahī an ākula fī hādhihi al-sāʿati fa-qālat ḥaddithnī bi-mā tamma laka al-yawma wa-mālaka mahmūmun wa-maksūru al-khāṭiri wa-al-qalbi
sentences.l: And-I-said: I-do-not-desire that I-eat in this the-hour. And-she-said: Tell-me of-what has-befallen to-you the-day, and-what-(is)-to-you, worried, and-broken-of the-mind and-the-heart?
sentences.i: I said, "I have no wish to eat at this hour." "Then tell me what has happened to you today," she said, "and why are you so anxious, broken in mind and heart?"
sentences.n: هَذِةِ is spelled with tāʾ marbūṭa, where Classical writes هَذِهِ; it is read hādhihi. وَمَالَكَ مَهْمُومٌ keeps the nominative where Classical would put مَهْمُومًا after مَا لَكَ. مَكْسُورُالْخَاطِرِ is two words run together: مَكْسُورُ الْخَاطِرِ, "broken of mind", the Arabic for crestfallen.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ السَّاعَةَ أُحَدِّثُكِ عَلَى مَهَلِي فَقَدَّمَتْ لِي الشَّرَابَ وَقَالَتْ دُونَكَ فَإِنَّهُ يُزِيلُ هَمَّكَ فَلَا بُدَّأَنْ تَشْرَبَ وَتُحَدِّثَنِي بِخَبَرِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu al-sāʿata uḥaddithuki ʿalā mahalī fa-qaddamat lī al-sharāba wa-qālat dūnaka fa-innahu yuzīlu hammaka fa-lā budda an tashraba wa-tuḥaddithanī bi-khabarika
sentences.l: And-I-said: The-hour I-tell-you, at my-leisure. And-she-presented to-me the-drink, and-said: Here-you-are, for-it removes your-care; so-no escape-that you-drink and-you-tell-me of-your-news.
sentences.i: "Presently I will tell you, in my own time," I said. She handed me the drink and said, "Here, take it, for it chases away your care. You must drink, and you must tell me your story."
sentences.n: السَّاعَةَ is "this hour", hence "in a little while, presently". دُونَكَ is the "here you are" imperative: "take it". فَلَا بُدَّانْ is فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ run together, "there is no escaping that", so "you must".

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا لَا بُدَّأَنْ أُحَدِّثَكِ قَالَتْ نَعَمْ فَقُلْتُ إِنْ كَانَ وَلَابُدَّ فَاسْقِينِي بِيَدِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā lā budda an uḥaddithaki qālat naʿam fa-qultu in kāna wa-lā budda fa-isqinī bi-yadiki
sentences.l: And-I-said to-her: No escape-that I-tell-you. She-said: Yes. And-I-said: If it-be, and-no-escape, then-give-me-to-drink with-your-hand.
sentences.i: I said to her, "I must tell you." "Yes," she said. So I said, "Then, if it must be, give me to drink with your own hand."

sentences.t: فَمَلَأَتِ الْقَدَحَ وَشَرِبَتْهُ وَمَلَأَتْهُ وَنَاوَلَتْنِي إِيَّاهُ فَتَنَاوَلْتُهُ مِنْهَا بِيَدِي الشِّمَالِ وَفَرَّتِ الدُّمُوعُ مِنْ جَفْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-malaʾati al-qadaḥa wa-sharibathu wa-malaʾathu wa-nāwalatnī iyyāhu fa-tanāwaltuhu minhā bi-yadī al-shimāli wa-farrati al-dumūʿu min jafnī
sentences.l: And-she-filled the-cup, and-drank-it, and-filled-it, and-handed-me it, and-I-took-it from-her with-my-hand the-left; and-fled the-tears from my-eyelid.
sentences.i: So she filled the cup, drank from it, filled it again and handed it to me; I took it from her with my left hand, and tears sprang from my eyes.
sentences.n: The verbs have no marked subject: I take the drinking (وَشَرِبَتْهُ) to be hers, a first draught to honour him, since the next clause turns to him with فَتَنَاوَلْتُهُ; but وَشَرِبْتُهُ, "and I drank it", is also possible. فَرَّتِ الدُّمُوعُ is literally "the tears fled"; the form may stand for فَارَتْ "welled up", which would give the same picture.

sentences.t: فَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُ—ولُ
sentences.tr: fa-anshadtu aqū—lu
sentences.l: And-I-recited, I-say:
sentences.i: Then I recited, saying:
sentences.n: The dash inside اقول is a printer's artefact (the print breaks the word); the word is اَقُولُ "I say", and فَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُولُ "I recited, saying" is the usual lead-in to a poem.

sentences.t:
اَذَا ارَادَ اللّٰهُ اَمْرًا لِامْرِاً * وَكَانَ ذَاعَقْلٍ وَسَمْعٍ وَبَصَرْ
اَصَمَّ اُذْنَاهُ وَاَعْمَى قَلْبَهُ * وَسَلَّ مِنْهُ عَقْلَهُ سَلَّ الشَّعَرْ
حَتَّى اِذَا انْفَلَّ فِيهِ حُكْمُهُ * رَدَّ اِلَيْهِ عَقْلَهُ لِيَعْتَبِرْ
sentences.tr:
adhā arāda Allāhu amran li-amriʾan * wa-kāna dhā ʿaqlin wa-samʿin wa-baṣar
aṣamma udhnāhu wa-aʿmā qalbahu * wa-salla minhu ʿaqlahu salla al-shaʿar
ḥattā idhā infalla fīhi ḥukmuhu * radda ilayhi ʿaqlahu li-yaʿtabir
sentences.i: When God wills some matter for a man, though he be endowed with mind, hearing and sight, He deafens his ears, blinds his heart, and draws his reason out of him as one draws a hair from dough; until, when His decree has run its course in him, He gives him back his reason, that he may take warning.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied as printed, including its irregular forms: اَذَا for إِذَا, لِامْرِاً for لِامْرِئٍ "for a man" (the print spells the accusative ending on the alif), and اُذْنَاهُ with the nominative dual where the syntax wants the accusative اُذْنَيْهِ. سَلَّ الشَّعَرْ "as a hair is drawn out" refers to the old proverb of drawing a hair out of dough, which comes away clean. انْفَلَّ is obscure: it means "was notched, broken", and I give "has run its course" for want of better; very likely the print stands for انْفَذَّ or نَفَذَ, "was carried out", which gives the same sense.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغْتُ مِنْ شِعْرِي تَنَاوَلْتُ الْقَدَحَ بِيَدِيَ الشِّمَالِ وَبَكَيْتُ وَصَرَخْتُ هِيَ صَرْخَةٌ قَوِيَّةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghtu min shiʿrī tanāwaltu al-qadaḥa bi-yadiya al-shimāli wa-bakaytu wa-ṣarakhtu hiya ṣarkhatun qawiyyatun
sentences.l: And-when I-finished from my-poetry, I-took the-cup in-my-hand the-left, and-I-wept and-I-cried-out; it-was a-cry strong.
sentences.i: When I had finished my verses, I took the cup in my left hand, and I wept and cried out, a loud and piercing cry.
sentences.n: هِيَ صَرْخَةٌ قَوِيَّةٌ is a bare appositive: the print gives هي ("it/she") where a verb or a plain noun phrase would be expected; read as "it was a strong cry".

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ مَا سَبَبُ بُكَاءِكَ أَحْرَقْتَ قَلْبِي وَمَالَكَ تَنَاوَلْتَ الْقَدَحَ بِيَدِكَ الشِّمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat mā sababu bukāʾika aḥraqta qalbī wa-mālaka tanāwalta al-qadaḥa bi-yadika al-shimāli
sentences.l: And-said-she: What cause of-your-weeping? You-burned my-heart! And-what-to-you you-took the-cup in-your-hand the-left?
sentences.i: She said, "What is the cause of your weeping? You have wounded my heart! And what ails you, that you take the cup in your left hand?"
sentences.n: The print writes ما لك ("what is the matter with you") as one word, وَمَالَكَ. The lone ء in بكاءك is printed as a letter, so it carries the vowel itself: bukāʾi-ka.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا إِنَّ فِي يَدِي حَبَّةً فَقَالَتْ أَخْرِجْهَا أَفْقَعْهَا لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā inna fī yadī ḥabbatan fa-qālat akhrijhā afqaʿhā laka
sentences.l: So-I-said to-her: Indeed in my-hand a-boil. So-said-she: Bring-it-out, I-may-burst-it for-you.
sentences.i: I said to her, "There is a boil in my hand." She said, "Bring it out, and let me lance it for you."
sentences.n: أَفْقَعْهَا is pointed as a jussive, the usual sequel to an imperative ("bring it out — that I may burst it"); the print gives no vowels, so this is our reading.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ مَا هُوَ وَقْتُ فَقْعِهَا فَلَا تُطِيلِي عَلَيَّ فَمَا أُخْرِجُ يَدِي فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu mā huwa waqtu faqʿihā fa-lā tuṭīlī ʿalayya fa-mā ukhriju yadī fī tilka al-sāʿati
sentences.l: So-I-said: Not it time of-its-bursting; so-do-not lengthen upon-me; so-not I-bring-out my-hand at that the-hour.
sentences.i: I said, "This is no time for lancing it. Do not press me, for I will not bring out my hand just now."

sentences.t: ثُمَّ شَرِبْتُ الْقَدَحَ وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تَسْقِينِي حَتَّى غَلَبَ عَلَيَّ السُّكْرُ فَنِمْتُ مَكَانِي
sentences.tr: thumma sharibtu al-qadaḥa wa-lam tazal tasqīnī ḥattā ghalaba ʿalayya al-sukru fa-nimtu makānī
sentences.l: Then I-drank the-cup, and-not she-ceased giving-me-to-drink until overcame upon-me the-drunkenness, so-I-slept in-my-place.
sentences.i: Then I drank the cup, and she kept on pouring for me until drunkenness overcame me, and I fell asleep where I sat.

sentences.t: فَأَبْصَرَتْ يَدِيَ بِلَاكَفٍّ فَفَتَّشَتْنِي فَرَأَتْ مَعِيَ الْكِيسَ بِالذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-abṣarat yadiya bi-lā kaffin fa-fattashatnī fa-raʾat maʿiya al-kīsa bi-al-dhahabi
sentences.l: So-she-saw my-hand without-palm; so-she-searched-me, and-she-saw with-me the-purse with-the-gold.
sentences.i: She saw that my hand had no palm; then she searched me and found on me the purse full of gold.
sentences.n: بلاكف is printed as a single word, بِلَا كَفٍّ, "without a hand". The man's right hand was cut off (the reason he eats and drinks with his left).

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْحُزْنِ مَالَا يَدْخُلُ عَلَى أَحَدٍ وَلَا زَالَتْ تَتَأَ لَّمُ بِسَبَبِي إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿalayhā mina al-ḥuzni mā lā yadkhulu ʿalā aḥadin wa-lā zālat tatāʾa lammu bi-sababī ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: So-entered upon-her, of the-sorrow, what not enters upon anyone; and-not she-ceased she-suffers because-of-me until the-morning.
sentences.i: Such grief came over her as comes over no one, and she went on suffering on my account until morning.
sentences.n: Print artefacts: مالا is مَا لَا run together ("what does not"); تتا لم is one verb, تَتَأَلَّمُ, broken by a space (tataʾallamu). ولا زالت is a Classical blessing-formula ("may she not cease") used here, Middle Arabic fashion, where Classical would say وما زالت.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَقْتُ مِنَ النَّوْمِ وَجَدْتُهَا هَيَّأَتْ لِي مَسْلُوقَةً وَقَدَّمَتْهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ أَرْبَعَةُ أَطْيَارٍ دَجَاجٍ وَسَقَتْنِي قَدَحَ شَرَابٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afaqtu mina al-nawmi wajadtuhā hayyaʾat lī maslūqatan wa-qaddamathā fa-idhā hiya arbaʿatu aṭyārin dajājin wa-saqatnī qadaḥa sharābin
sentences.l: And-when I-awoke from the-sleep, I-found-her she-had-prepared for-me a-boiled-thing, and-she-presented-it; and-behold it four birds, chickens; and-she-gave-me-to-drink a-cup of-drink.
sentences.i: When I woke from my sleep I found that she had prepared a boiled dish for me. She set it before me, and there were four fowls, chickens, and she gave me a cup of wine to drink.
sentences.n: هيات is printed without the hamza-seat that Classical spelling would give (هَيَّأَتْ); مَسْلُوقَةً is a feminine participle used as a noun, "a boiled thing". شراب, "drink", is the Nights' ordinary word for wine.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْتُ وَشَرِبْتُ وَحَطَّيْتُ الْكِيسَ وَأَرَدْتُ الْخُرُوجَ فَقَالَتْ لِي إِلَى أَيْنَ رَائِعٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akaltu wa-sharibtu wa-ḥaṭṭaytu al-kīsa wa-aradtu al-khurūja fa-qālat lī ilā ayna rāʾiʿun
sentences.l: So-I-ate and-I-drank and-I-put-down the-purse and-I-wanted the-going-out; so-said-she to-me: To where, startled-one?
sentences.i: I ate and drank, put the purse in place, and made to go out. She said to me, "Where to, in such a fright?"
sentences.n: رائع is printed so, and is read here as "startled, alarmed"; it may be a misprint for رائح, "going off", which would suit the next line (لا ترح, "do not go"). حطيت is the colloquial form of Classical حططتُ.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ أَذْهَبُ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَتْ لَا تَرُحْ اجْلِسْ فَجَلَسْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu ilā makānin adhhabu ilayhi fa-qālat lā taruḥ ijlis fa-jalastu
sentences.l: So-I-said: To a-place I-go to-it. So-said-she: Do-not go-off; sit. So-I-sat.
sentences.i: I said, "To a place I must go to." She said, "Do not go. Sit down." And I sat.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَبَلَغَتْ مَحَبَّتُكَ أَنْ صَرَفْتَ جَمِيعَ مَالِكَ وَعَدِمْتَ كَفَّكَ أُشْهِدُكَ عَلَيَّ وَالشَّاهِدُ اللَّهُ أَنِّي لَا أُفَارِقُكَ وَسَتَرَى صِحَّةَ قَوْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-balaghat maḥabbatuka an ṣarafta jamīʿa mālika wa-ʿadimta kaffaka ushhiduka ʿalayya wa-al-shāhidu Allāhu annī lā ufāriquka wa-sa-tarā ṣiḥḥata qawlī
sentences.l: So-said-she: And-reached your-love that you-spent all of-your-wealth and-you-lost your-palm. I-make-witness-you upon-me, and-the-witness God, that-I not I-part-from-you; and-will-you-see the-soundness of-my-saying.
sentences.i: She said, "Your love has gone so far that you have spent all your wealth and lost your hand. I call you to witness against myself, and God is the witness, that I will never part from you. You will see that my word is true."
sentences.n: أُشْهِدُكَ عَلَيَّ is a little elliptical: "I make you witness over me", that is, "I bind myself before you".

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَتْ خَلْفَ الشُّهُودِ فَحَضَرُوا
sentences.tr: wa-arsalat khalfa al-shuhūdi fa-ḥaḍarū
sentences.l: And-she-sent behind the-witnesses, and-they-attended.
sentences.i: She sent for the witnesses, and they came.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُمُ اكْتُبُو اكِتَابِي عَلَى هَذَا الشَّابِّ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي قَبَضْتُ الْمَهْرَ فَكَتَبُوا كِتَابِي غَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahumu uktubū ikitābī ʿalā hādhā al-shābbi wa-ishhadū annī qabaḍtu al-mahra fa-katabū kitābī ghalayhā
sentences.l: So-said-she to-them: Write my-contract upon this the-youth, and-witness that-I received the-bride-price. So-they-wrote my-contract to-her.
sentences.i: She said to them, "Draw up my marriage contract with this young man, and bear witness that I have received the dower." So they wrote my contract with her.
sentences.n: Print slips: اكتبو lacks its final alif, which has slipped onto the next word, so that اكتابي stands for كتابي ("my contract"); غليها is a misprint for عليها, "with/to her". Both are kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتِ اشْهَدُوا أَنَّ جَمِيعَ مَالِى الَّذِي فِي هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقِ وَجَمِيعَ مَا عِنْدِي مِنَ الْعَبِيدِ وَالْجَوَارِ لِهَذَا الشَّابِّ
sentences.tr: thumma qālati ishhadū anna jamīʿa mālī alladhī fī hādhā al-ṣundūqi wa-jamīʿa mā ʿindī mina al-ʿabīdi wa-al-jawāri li-hādhā al-shābbi
sentences.l: Then said-she: Witness that all of-my-wealth that in this the-chest, and-all what with-me of the-slaves and-the-slave-girls, belongs to-this the-youth.
sentences.i: Then she said, "Bear witness that all my wealth in this chest, and all that I have of male slaves and slave girls, belongs to this young man."
sentences.n: الجوار is printed without the final yā of الجواري ("the slave girls"); read as the defective plural, genitive after مِنْ.

sentences.t: فَشَهِدُوا عَلَيْهَا وَقَبِلْتُ أَنَا التَّمْلِيكَ وَانْصَرَفُوا بَعْدَ مَا أَخَذُوا الْأُجْرَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-shahidū ʿalayhā wa-qabiltu anā al-tamlīka wa-inṣarafū baʿda mā akhadhū al-ujrata
sentences.l: So-they-testified upon-her, and-I-accepted I the-conveyance, and-they-departed after what they-took the-fee.
sentences.i: They bore witness against her, and I accepted the transfer of ownership; then the witnesses left, after taking their fee.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَتْنِي مِنْ يَدِي وَأَوْقَفَتْنِي عَلَى خِزَانَةٍ وَفَتَحَتْ صُنْدُوقًا كَبِيرًا وَقَالَتْ لِي انْظُرْ إِلَى الَّذِي فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ فَنَظَرْتُ فَإِذَا هُوَ مَلْأَنُ مِنَا دِيلَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhatnī min yadī wa-awqafatnī ʿalā khizānatin wa-fataḥat ṣundūqan kabīran wa-qālat lī unẓur ilā alladhī fī al-ṣundūqi fa-naẓartu fa-idhā huwa malʾanu manā dīla
sentences.l: And-she-took-me from my-hand, and-she-made-me-stand upon a-cabinet, and-she-opened a-chest, big, and-she-said to-me: Look at the-which in the-chest. So-I-looked, and-behold, it (was) full of-handkerchiefs.
sentences.i: She took me by the hand and stood me before a cupboard, then opened a large chest and said to me, "Look at what is inside the chest." I looked, and behold, it was brimming with handkerchiefs.
sentences.n: مَلْأَنُ is the print's spelling for مَلْآنُ "full", with its hamza as printed. The edition breaks مَنَادِيلَ "handkerchiefs" into two words, مَنَا and دِيلَ; I point each half so that read together they give the one word. The speaker in these lines is the young man, telling the Christian what befell him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ هَذَا مَالُكَ الَّذِي أَخَذْتُهُ مِنْكَ فَكُلَّمَا أَعْطَيْتَنِي مِنْدِيلًا فِيهِ خَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا أُولِّفُهُ وَأَرْمِيهِ فِي هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقِ فَخُذْ مَالَكَ فَقَدْ رَجَعَ إِلَيْكَ وَأَنْتَ الْيَوْمَ عَزِيرٌ فَقَدْ جَرَى عَلَيْكَ الْقَضَاءُ بِسَبَبِي حَتَّى عَدِمْتَ يَمِينَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat hādhā māluka alladhī akhadhtuhu minka fa-kullamā aʿṭaytanī mindīlan fīhi khamsīna dīnāran uwallifuhu wa-armīhi fī hādhā al-ṣundūqi fa-khudh mālaka fa-qad rajaʿa ilayka wa-anta al-yawma ʿazīrun fa-qad jarā ʿalayka al-qaḍāʾu bi-sababī ḥattā ʿadimta yamīnaka
sentences.l: So-she-said: This (is) your-wealth which I-took from-you. So-every-time you-gave-me a-handkerchief, in-it fifty dinars, I-would-bundle-it and-throw-it into this chest. So take your-wealth, for-it has returned to-you, and-you (are) today dear. For-the-decree has-run upon-you through my-cause, until you-lost your-right-hand.
sentences.i: She said, "This is your money that I took from you. Every time you gave me a handkerchief with fifty dinars in it, I bundled it up and threw it into this chest. So take back your money, for it has returned to you, and today you are a dear man to me. Fate has struck you on my account, so that you lost your right hand."
sentences.n: عَزِيرٌ is printed with ر where عَزِيزٌ "dear, precious" is expected; I point it as the sense requires and take the ر as a slip of the print. أُولِّفُهُ is printed with أو; it is probably meant for أُؤَلِّفُهُ "I would put it together, bundle it", a habitual present after كُلَّمَا. The tr here is a plain rendering of the letters as pointed.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا لَا أَقْدِرُا كَافِئَكَ وَلَوْ بَذَلْتُ رُوحِي لَكَانَ قَلِيلًا وَلَكَ الْفَضْلُ
sentences.tr: wa-anā lā aqdiru ukāfiʾaka wa-law badhaltu rūḥī la-kāna qalīlan wa-laka al-faḍlu
sentences.l: And-I not I-am-able, I-repay-you; and-if I-spent my-spirit, it-would-be little; and-to-you (belongs) the-favour.
sentences.i: I cannot repay you, and were I to give up my very soul it would be little; the favour is yours.
sentences.n: The print has اقدرا كافئك, with a stray alif on the first word; the alif belongs to the verb that follows, أُكَافِئَكَ "that I repay you". I keep the alif where it is printed and read the pair as أَقْدِرُ أُكَافِئَكَ, the bare juxtaposition of two verbs that the Middle Arabic of the Nights likes.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِي تَسَلَّمْ مَالَكَ فَنَقَلْتُ صُنْدُوقَهَا إِلَى صُنْدُوقِي وَجَعَلْتُ مَالِي إِلَى مَالِهَا الَّذِي كُنْتُ أَعْطَيْتُهُ لَهَا وَفَرِحَ قَلْبِي وَزَالَ هَمِّي فَقُمْتُ قَبَّلْتُهَا وَشَكَرْتُ لَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lī tasallam mālaka fa-naqaltu ṣundūqahā ilā ṣundūqī wa-jaʿaltu mālī ilā mālihā alladhī kuntu aʿṭaytuhu lahā wa-fariḥa qalbī wa-zāla hammī fa-qumtu qabbaltuhā wa-shakartu lahā
sentences.l: Then she-said to-me: Take-possession-of your-wealth. So-I-moved her-chest to my-chest, and-I-placed my-wealth with her-wealth which I-had given to-her; and-rejoiced my-heart and-passed-away my-worry. So-I-rose, I-kissed-her, and-I-thanked to-her.
sentences.i: Then she said to me, "Take your wealth." So I moved her chest across to mine and put my money together with her money, the money I had given her. My heart rejoiced and my worry vanished; I got up, kissed her and thanked her.
sentences.n: فَقُمْتُ قَبَّلْتُهَا puts two verbs side by side with no وَ between them, as colloquial narration does: "I rose, I kissed her". كُنْتُ أَعْطَيْتُهُ is the Middle Arabic way of saying "which I had given"; Classical would add قَدْ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَقَدْ بَذَلْتَ يَدَكَ فِي مَحَبَّتِي فَكَيْفَ أَقْدِرُ عَلَى مُكَافَأَتِكَ وَاللَّهِ لَوْبَذَلْتُ رُوحِي فِي مَحَبَّتِكَ لَكَانَ قَلِيلًا وَمَا أَقُومُ بِوَاجِبِ حَقِّكَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat la-qad badhalta yadaka fī maḥabbatī fa-kayfa aqdiru ʿalā mukāfaʾatika wa-Allāhi lawbadhaltu rūḥī fī maḥabbatika la-kāna qalīlan wa-mā aqūmu bi-wājibi ḥaqqika ʿalayya
sentences.l: So-she-said: Indeed you-spent your-hand in my-love; so how am-I-able upon your-repaying? By-God, if-I-spent my-spirit in your-love, it-would-be little; and-I-do-not stand with-the-due of-your-right upon me.
sentences.i: She said, "You gave up your hand for love of me, so how can I ever repay you? By God, were I to give up my soul for love of you, it would still be little, and I would not have discharged what I owe you."
sentences.n: لَوْبَذَلْتُ is printed as one word, لو and بذلت run together. مُكَافَأَتِكَ is printed مكافاتك, without a visible hamza; I add it above the second alif. وَاجِبُ حَقِّكَ is "what is due to your claim", the debt she owes him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا كَتَبَتْ لِي جَمِيعَ مَا تَمْلِكُ مِنْ ثِيَابِ بَدَنِهَا وَصِيغَتِهَا وَأَسْبَا بِهَا بِحُجَّةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā katabat lī jamīʿa mā tamliku min thiyābi badanihā wa-ṣīghatihā wa-asbā bihā bi-ḥujjatin
sentences.l: Then indeed-she wrote to-me the-whole of-what she-owns, from clothes-of her-body and-her-jewellery and-her-effects, by-a-deed.
sentences.i: Then she made over to me, by a written deed, everything she owned: the clothes off her back, her jewellery and all her effects.
sentences.n: The print splits وَأَسْبَابِهَا "and her effects (belongings)" into واسبا and بها; I point the halves so that together they read as the one word. أَسْبَاب, plural of سَبَب, here means the means and gear she has. حُجَّة is a legal deed or instrument.

sentences.t: وَمَا نَامَتْ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ إِلَّا مَهْمُومَةً مِنْ هَمِّي حَتَّى حَكَيْتُ لَهَا جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لِي وَبِتُّ مَعَهَا وَأَقَمْنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْ شَهْرٍ وَقَوِيَ بِهَا الضَّعْفُ وَزَادَ بِهَا الْمَرَضُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā nāmat tilka al-layla illā mahmūmatan min hammī ḥattā ḥakaytu lahā jamīʿa mā waqaʿa lī wa-bittu maʿahā wa-aqamnā aqalla min shahrin wa-qawiya bihā al-ḍaʿfu wa-zāda bihā al-maraḍu
sentences.l: And-she-did-not sleep that night except worried from my-worry, until I-told to-her the-whole of-what befell to-me; and-I-spent-the-night with-her; and-we-stayed less than a-month, and-grew-strong upon-her the-weakness, and-increased upon-her the-sickness.
sentences.i: That night she did not sleep, so troubled was she by my trouble, until I had told her all that had befallen me; and I passed the night with her. We stayed less than a month, and her weakness grew stronger and her sickness worse.
sentences.n: قَوِيَ بِهَا الضَّعْفُ is literally "weakness grew strong with her": the weakness gets the better of her. مَهْمُومَةً مِنْ هَمِّي plays on her being worried (مَهْمُومَة) by his worry (هَمّ).

sentences.t: وَلَا مَكَثَتْ غَيْرَ خَمْسِينَ يَوْمًا إِلَّا وَهِيَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْآخِرَةِ فَجَهَّزْتُهَا وَوَارَيْتُهَا التُّرَابَ وَعَمِلْتُ لَهَا خَتْمَاتٍ وَتَصَدَّقْتُ عَلَيْهَا بِجُمْلَةٍ مِنَ الْمَالِ وَنَزَلْتُ مِنَ التُّرْبَةِ فَرَأَيْتُ لَهَا مَالًا جَزِيلًا وَأَمْلَاكًا وَعَقَارَاتٍ وَمِنْ جُمْلَةِ تِلْكَ الْمَخَازِنِ مَخْزَنُ السِّمْسِمِ الَّذِي بِعْتُ لَكَ مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lā makathat ghayra khamsīna yawman illā wa-hiya min ahli al-ākhirati fa-jahhaztuhā wa-wāraytuhā al-turāba wa-ʿamiltu lahā khatamātin wa-taṣaddaqtu ʿalayhā bi-jumlatin min al-māli wa-nazaltu min al-turbati fa-raʾaytu lahā mālan jazīlan wa-amlākan wa-ʿaqārātin wa-min jumlati tilka al-makhāzini makhzanu al-simsimi alladhī biʿtu laka minhu
sentences.l: And-not she-stayed other-than fifty days except and-she (was) of the-people-of the-Hereafter. So-I-prepared-her, and-I-covered-her the-dust, and-I-made for-her recitations-of-the-whole-Qurʾan, and-I-gave-alms on-her-behalf of-a-sum of the-wealth, and-I-went-down from the-graveyard. And-I-saw of-hers wealth, abundant, and-estates and-properties; and from the-sum-of those storehouses (was) the-storehouse-of the-sesame which I-sold to-you from-it.
sentences.i: She lingered no more than fifty days before she was among the people of the Hereafter. I prepared her for burial and covered her with the earth; I had the Qurʾan recited through for her several times, and gave a great sum in alms for her soul. Then I came down from the graveyard and went through what she had left: abundant wealth, estates and landed properties, and among those storehouses was the sesame store from which I had sold to you.
sentences.n: مِنْ أَهْلِ الْآخِرَةِ, "of the people of the Hereafter", is the polite way to say she was dead. خَتْمَات are complete recitations of the Qurʾan, ordered for the dead. لَا مَكَثَتْ ... إِلَّا وَهِيَ is a negative-then-exception frame, "she had not stayed fifty days before she was". The speaker turns to the Christian: لَكَ is you, the sesame merchant, who sold him the sesame.

sentences.t: وَمَاكَانَ اشْتِغَالِي عَنْكَ هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةَ حَتَّى بِعْتُ بَقِيَّةَ الْحَوَاصِلِ وَجَمِيعَ مَا فِى الْمَخَازِنِ وَإِلَى الْآنَ لَمْ أَفْرُغْ مِنْ قَبْضِ الثَّمَنِ
sentences.tr: wa-mākāna ishtighālī ʿanka hādhihi al-muddata ḥattā biʿtu baqiyyata al-ḥawāṣili wa-jamīʿa mā fī al-makhāzini wa-ilā al-āni lam afrugh min qabḍi al-thamani
sentences.l: And-was-not my-being-busy away-from-you this the-period until I-sold the-remainder-of the-stores and-the-whole-of what (is) in the-storehouses; and until now I-have-not finished from receiving the-price.
sentences.i: That is why I was kept from you all this time, selling off the rest of the stock and everything in the storehouses; and even now I have not finished collecting the money.
sentences.n: مَاكَانَ is printed as one word. The sentence is "my absence from you was only until I had sold": the speaker explains why he has been away, busy with the dead woman's goods. الْحَوَاصِل are stored goods and produce.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّكَ لَا تُخَالِفُنِي فِيمَا أَقُولُ لَكَ عَلَيْهِ لِأَنِّي أَكَلْتُ زَادَكَ وَقَدْ وَهَبْتُكَ ثَمَنَ السِّمْسِمِ الَّذِي عِنْدَكَ فَهَذَا سَبَبُ قَطْعِ يَمِينِي وَأَكْلِي بِيَدِي الشِّمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-innaka lā tukhālifunī fīmā aqūlu laka ʿalayhi li-annī akaltu zādaka wa-qad wahabtuka thamana al-simsimi alladhī ʿindaka fa-hādhā sababu qaṭʿi yamīnī wa-aklī bi-yadī al-shimāli
sentences.l: And-indeed-you not you-oppose-me in-what I-say to-you about-it, because I-ate your-provisions; and-I-have given-you the-price-of the-sesame which (is) with-you. So this (is) the-cause-of the-cutting-of my-right-hand and-my-eating with-my-hand the-left.
sentences.i: And you must not oppose me in what I say to you about this, for I have eaten your provisions, and I have given you the price of the sesame that is in your hands. This, then, is why my right hand was cut off, and why I eat with my left.
sentences.n: The opening وَإِنَّكَ لَا تُخَالِفُنِي is loose: it reads as "and (see that) you do not oppose me", a request that the Christian accept the money without argument; the print may mean وَأَنْ لَا. عَلَيْهِ after أَقُولُ is "about it". بِيَدِي الشِّمَالِ is "with my hand, the left", an apposition rather than a Classical idāfa.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَقَدْ أَحْسَنْتَ وَتَفَضَّلْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu la-qad aḥsanta wa-tafaḍḍalta
sentences.l: So-I-said to-him: Indeed you-did-well and-you-showed-favour.
sentences.i: I said to him, "You have done well, and shown great kindness."
sentences.n: From here the voice is the Christian broker's, answering the young man.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تُسَافِرَ مَعِى إِلَى بِلَادِي فَإِنِّي اشْتَرَيْتُ مَتْجَرًا مِصْرِيًّا وَإِسْكَنْدَرَانِيًّا فَهَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تُصَاحِبَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī hal laka an tusāfira maʿī ilā bilādī fa-innī ishtaraytu matjaran miṣriyyan wa-iskandarāniyyan fa-hal laka an tuṣāḥibanī
