sentences.l: So-he-said to-me: Is-there for-you that you-travel with-me to my-lands? For-I bought merchandise, Egyptian and-Alexandrian; so is-there for-you that you-accompany-me?
sentences.i: He said to me, "Would you like to travel with me to my country? I have bought Egyptian and Alexandrian merchandise. Will you keep me company?"
sentences.n: هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ is "do you have it in you to...?", an idiom of invitation. مَتْجَر is merchandise, trade goods.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ وَأَوْعَدْتُهُ عَلَى رَأْسِ الشَّهْرِ ثُمَّ بِعْتُ جَمِيعَ مَا أَمْلِكُ وَاشْتَرَيْتُ بِهِ مَتْجَرًا آخَرَ وَسَافَرْتُ أَنَا وَالشَّابُّ إِلَى هَذِهِ الْبِلَادِ الَّتِي هِيَ بِلَادُكُمْ فَبَاعَ الشَّابُّ مَتْجَرَهُ وَاشْتَرَى عِوَضَهُ مِنْ بِلَادِكُمْ وَمَضَى إِلَى دِيَارِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu naʿam wa-awʿadtuhu ʿalā raʾsi al-shahri thumma biʿtu jamīʿa mā amliku wa-ishtaraytu bihi matjaran ākhara wa-sāfartu anā wa-al-shābbu ilā hādhihi al-bilādi allatī hiya bilādukum fa-bāʿa al-shābbu matjarahu wa-ishtarā ʿiwaḍahu min bilādikum wa-maḍā ilā diyāri al-miṣriyyati
sentences.l: So-I-said: Yes. And-I-made-an-appointment-with-him at the-head-of the-month. Then I-sold the-whole-of what I-own, and-I-bought with-it merchandise, other; and-I-travelled, I and-the-young-man, to these the-lands which (are) your-lands. So-sold the-young-man his-merchandise, and-bought in-exchange-for-it from your-lands, and-went-away to the-abodes-of the-Egyptian.
sentences.i: I said, "Yes," and we fixed a day at the turn of the month. Then I sold all that I owned and bought other merchandise with it, and I travelled, I and the young man, to this country, which is your country. The young man sold his goods and bought goods of your land in exchange, and went back to the lands of Egypt.
sentences.n: وَأَوْعَدْتُهُ is Form IV where Classical has وَاعَدْتُهُ "I made an appointment with him". عَلَى رَأْسِ الشَّهْرِ is "at the head of the month", at the month's turning. دِيَارِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ puts a definite adjective after a construct noun, "the Egyptian lands"; Classical would say دِيَارِ مِصْرَ.

sentences.t: فَكَانَ قِسْمِي أَنَا فِي قُعَادِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ حَتَّى حَصَلَ مَا حَصَلَ لِي فِي غُرْبَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-kāna qismī anā fī quʿādī hādhihi al-layla ḥattā ḥaṣala mā ḥaṣala lī fī ghurbatī
sentences.l: So-was my-portion, I, in my-sitting this the-night, until happened what happened to-me in my-exile.
sentences.i: As for me, my lot was to stay on here tonight, until there befell me in my exile what has befallen me.
sentences.n: قُعَادِي is the Middle Arabic verbal noun "my staying, sitting" (Classical قُعُودِي). The sentence is deliberately roundabout: he has stayed in this city, and the events that landed him before the king followed from that.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا يَامَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ مَا هُوَ أَعْجَبُ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā yāmalika al-zamāni mā huwa aʿjabu min ḥadīthi al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: So this, O-king-of the-time, is-it more-wondrous than the-tale-of the-hunchback?
sentences.i: So tell me, O king of the age: is this more wondrous than the tale of the Hunchback?
sentences.n: يَامَلِكَ is printed as one word. The print has no question mark; مَا هُوَ أَعْجَبُ is read as a question, "is it not more wondrous than...?", asking the king to judge.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ لَابُدَّ مِنْ شَنْقِكُمْ كُلِّكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku lābudda min shanqikum kullikum
sentences.l: So-said the-king: There-is-no-escape from hanging-you, all-of-you.
sentences.i: But the king said, "There is no help for it: I must hang every one of you."
sentences.n: لَابُدَّ is printed as one word. The king gives no weight to the tale's wonder and holds to his sentence.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَ—ا—حِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-mub—ā—ḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazad the-morning, so-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: الْمُبَ—ا—حِ is the print's spelling of الْمُبَاحِ "the permitted", with a dash on each side of the alif; the dashes are a printing artefact. The formula is the usual night's end, "she fell silent from the permitted speech".
